frontier.hypothesis: A byte-free +1 reference on `i` (78) in the i-FIRST order closes the all-target-seats chassis outright: i needs >= 9 flow refs (2783 > tbl's 2553) and <= 11 (3402 < stptr's 3409), and everything else in rejected/tbl-symK-ilate-alltarget-seats-emission-swapped.c - including the 4 preamble insns the i-late spelling gets wrong - is already target.
frontier.mechanism: flow.c takes reg_n_refs before combine runs, so any `i` mention that is deleted by combine (rather than by cse1's constant propagation or flow's dead-store elimination) is a free +1; uses placed INSIDE loop1/loop2 cost nothing in live length by this session's loop-carried invariance law and are not constant-foldable there.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate combine-deletable `i` mentions inside the loops: exit tests whose compare operand is produced by a separate insn combine folds in (`if (i - 0x12 < 0)`, `if ((s32)(i - 0x14) < 0)`), an index/offset expression in a loop body that consumes i and is folded into an existing addiu, and a staged copy of i placed under the s7 canonicality rule (after every other i use in its block, single consumer). For each: .lreg reg_n_refs for 78 plus the insn count, then sandbox.

frontier.hypothesis: The preamble emission order can be attacked directly on the i-late (target-seat) spelling instead of the seats, since sched1 - not the allocator - is what puts the tbl pair first.
frontier.mechanism: sched1 ranks by INSN_PRIORITY (longest path to the end of the block) and breaks ties by LUID; both preamble defs are dependence-free within block 0, so the tie falls to RTL order. A block-0 consumer of `i` would raise the i pair's priority above the tbl pair's - but every block-0 use of i is constant-propagated by cse1 before flow and sched see it.
frontier.next_probe: Look for a block-0 consumer of i that cse1 cannot fold (its value not literally 1 at that point) and that costs no bytes, or conversely for a construct that lengthens the tbl pair's dependence path; dump .sched for the i-late chassis and read the ready-list order to confirm the tie-break before spelling anything.

frontier.hypothesis: The original never lifted tbl at all: rederive the source shape under the joint constraint 'out2 has >= 4 flow refs and exactly 3 materialised ones, with pri in (1473.7, 1702.1)' rather than perturbing the current body.
frontier.mechanism: H-s6-5 (target's s6 carries only three materialised references, so the 4th was deleted post-flow by combine) plus this session's finding that the tbl sym-K chain - our own invention, and a construct that would have to survive the cheat checklist - is the only thing forcing the i-vs-tbl fight.
frontier.next_probe: In `rederive` modality: m2c output plus target asm, deriving loop2's pointer structure from scratch (separate local, different loop1/loop2 split, or an a4 store/reload shape) under that constraint, instead of reusing the merged-stptr chassis every session in this ledger assumes.
